Association between each diet score (origin and NOVA) and the resistome.

* Outcomes and models are the same as in `0.-Diet_group/Scripts/01.Diet_models.Rmd`:
  ARG load = log(total CPM) (lm), richness (Poisson glm) and Simpson (lm).
* Scores are standardised (z), so effects are per 1-SD increase in times/day.
* Covariates: sex + age + BMI + log10 sequencing depth.
* p-values are BH-adjusted within each system (Origin, NOVA) and outcome.

Two sensitivity models are fitted alongside each main model, because they decide how the result should be read:

* **+ diet group, NOVA only.** Food processing is conceptually unrelated to the omnivore-vegetarian-vegan
  pattern (diet group explains ≤ 5.4 % of any NOVA score), so a NOVA score that survives the adjustment is a
  genuinely orthogonal axis of diet. The origin scores are **not** adjusted: the diet groups are defined by
  animal-food intake (diet group explains 56-67 % of the animal scores, and 95 % of vegans score 0 on animal
  primary), so adjusting one for the other enters the same variable twice and its loss of significance is
  expected by construction. Origin scores are read as the diet-group gradient in continuous form.
* **+ total intake** (the sum of all food times/day, identical whether added up by origin or by NOVA, since
  both partition the same 185 FFQ items). This answers the obvious objection that an association with a food
  group only reflects eating more in total.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

rm(list = ls())

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)

table_dir <- here("1.-FFQ_analysis", "Results", "Tables")
plot_dir <- here("1.-FFQ_analysis", "Results", "Plots")
dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```


```{r theme set, include=FALSE}
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()))

system_colors <- c(
  "Origin" = "#338040",
  "NOVA"   = "#4B1D6F")
```


# Data load

```{r data load}
analysis_data <- read_tsv(file.path(table_dir, "analysis_data.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
         diet_group = factor(diet_group, levels = c("Omnivore", "Vegetarian", "Vegan")))
score_info <- read_tsv(file.path(table_dir, "score_info.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Total intake: the six origin scores and the four NOVA groups are two partitions of the same FFQ,
# so either sum gives the same total. Checked rather than assumed.
origin_scores <- score_info$score[score_info$system == "Origin"]
nova_scores <- score_info$score[score_info$system == "NOVA"]
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(total_intake = rowSums(across(all_of(origin_scores))))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(analysis_data$total_intake,
                           rowSums(analysis_data[nova_scores]))))
cat("Total intake (times/day): median", round(median(analysis_data$total_intake), 1),
    "| range", paste(round(range(analysis_data$total_intake), 1), collapse = " - "), "\n")
```


# Models

```{r models}
covariates <- "sex + age + bmi + log10_depth"

outcomes <- tribble(
  ~outcome,       ~endpoint,       ~family,
  "log_ARG_load", "ARG load",      "gaussian",
  "richness",     "ARG richness",  "poisson",
  "simpson",      "ARG Simpson",   "gaussian")

fit_score_model <- function(score, outcome, family, extra = "") {
  model_df <- analysis_data %>%
    mutate(score_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[score]])),
           total_intake_z = as.numeric(scale(total_intake)))
  formula_i <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ score_z +", covariates, extra))
  fit <- glm(formula_i, data = model_df, family = family)
  # t quantile for linear models (as lm), normal quantile for Poisson
  crit <- if (family == "gaussian") qt(0.975, df.residual(fit)) else qnorm(0.975)

  tidy(fit) %>%
    filter(term == "score_z") %>%
    transmute(estimate, se = std.error, statistic, p_value = p.value,
              conf_low = estimate - crit * se,
              conf_high = estimate + crit * se,
              dispersion = sum(residuals(fit, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(fit),
              n = nobs(fit))
}

results <- expand_grid(score_info, outcomes) %>%
  mutate(fit = pmap(list(score, outcome, family), fit_score_model)) %>%
  unnest(fit) %>%
  group_by(system, endpoint) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Richness effects as incidence rate ratios
  mutate(across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
                ~ if_else(family == "poisson", exp(.x), .x)),
         effect = if_else(family == "poisson", "IRR", "beta"),
         p_signif = case_when(p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
                              p_adj < 0.01 ~ "**",
                              p_adj < 0.05 ~ "*",
                              TRUE ~ "ns"))
```

```{r dispersion}
results %>%
  filter(family == "poisson") %>%
  summarise(min_dispersion = min(dispersion), max_dispersion = max(dispersion))
```

```{r results}
results %>%
  filter(system != "NOVA (sensitivity)") %>%
  select(system, label, endpoint, effect, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, p_value, p_adj, p_signif) %>%
  arrange(endpoint, p_value) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```


# Sensitivity analysis

Same models with the foods flagged in the NOVA classification moved to NOVA 1.

```{r sensitivity}
results %>%
  filter(str_detect(system, "NOVA"), label %in% label[system == "NOVA (sensitivity)"]) %>%
  select(system, label, endpoint, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, p_adj) %>%
  arrange(endpoint, label, system) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## Is each score an axis of its own, or the diet-group gradient restated?

How much of each score the diet group already explains (R² of score ~ diet group). This decides which scores
can be adjusted for diet group: only those the groups do not define.

```{r collinearity with diet group}
diet_collinearity <- score_info %>%
  filter(system != "NOVA (sensitivity)") %>%
  mutate(r2_diet_group = map_dbl(score, ~ summary(lm(analysis_data[[.x]] ~ analysis_data$diet_group))$r.squared),
         vif = 1 / (1 - r2_diet_group),
         vegans_at_zero = map_dbl(score, ~ mean(analysis_data[[.x]][analysis_data$diet_group == "Vegan"] == 0)))
diet_collinearity %>% select(system, label, r2_diet_group, vif, vegans_at_zero) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

NOVA models are refitted adding the diet group; all models are refitted adding total intake.

```{r sensitivity models}
sensitivity <- expand_grid(score_info %>% filter(system != "NOVA (sensitivity)"), outcomes) %>%
  mutate(diet_adjusted = pmap(list(score, outcome, family, system),
                              function(score, outcome, family, system) {
                                if (system == "NOVA") fit_score_model(score, outcome, family, extra = "+ diet_group")
                                else tibble(estimate = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_)
                              }),
         intake_adjusted = pmap(list(score, outcome, family), fit_score_model, extra = "+ total_intake_z")) %>%
  transmute(system, score, label, endpoint, family,
            estimate_diet_adjusted = map_dbl(diet_adjusted, "estimate"),
            p_diet_adjusted = map_dbl(diet_adjusted, "p_value"),
            estimate_intake_adjusted = map_dbl(intake_adjusted, "estimate"),
            p_intake_adjusted = map_dbl(intake_adjusted, "p_value")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("estimate_"), ~ if_else(family == "poisson", exp(.x), .x))) %>%
  select(-family)

results <- results %>%
  left_join(sensitivity %>% select(-system, -label), by = c("score", "endpoint"))

results %>%
  filter(system != "NOVA (sensitivity)", p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  select(system, label, endpoint, estimate, p_adj,
         estimate_diet_adjusted, p_diet_adjusted, estimate_intake_adjusted, p_intake_adjusted) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(endpoint, p_adj) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

Total intake itself, as a reference: does eating more of anything predict the resistome?

```{r total intake}
map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(outcomes)), function(i) {
  fit <- glm(as.formula(paste(outcomes$outcome[i], "~ scale(total_intake) +", covariates)),
             data = analysis_data, family = outcomes$family[i])
  tidy(fit) %>% filter(str_detect(term, "total_intake")) %>%
    transmute(endpoint = outcomes$endpoint[i], estimate, p_value = p.value)
})

cat("Total intake by diet group (Kruskal p =",
    signif(kruskal.test(total_intake ~ diet_group, analysis_data)$p.value, 3), "):\n")
analysis_data %>% group_by(diet_group) %>% summarise(median_total_intake = median(total_intake))
```

## Correlation between the scores

The ten scores are not independent exposures: origin and NOVA partition the same questionnaire, and the
omnivore-to-vegan gradient moves several of them together.

```{r score correlations}
score_correlations <- analysis_data %>%
  select(all_of(c(origin_scores, nova_scores))) %>%
  cor(method = "spearman") %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "score")

score_correlations %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>% print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```


# Forest plot

```{r forest plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
plot_data <- results %>%
  filter(system != "NOVA (sensitivity)") %>%
  mutate(system = factor(system, levels = names(system_colors)),
         label = fct_rev(fct_inorder(label)),
         endpoint = factor(endpoint, levels = outcomes$endpoint),
         null_value = if_else(effect == "IRR", 1, 0))

plot_associations <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = estimate, y = label, colour = system)) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = null_value), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), width = 0.2, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = p_adj < 0.05), size = 2.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 16), labels = c("q ≥ 0.05", "q < 0.05"), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = system_colors, name = "Classification") +
  facet_grid(system ~ endpoint, scales = "free", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Effect per 1-SD increase (beta; IRR for richness)", y = NULL)

plot_associations
```


# Save

```{r save}
write_tsv(results %>% select(-family), file.path(table_dir, "score_associations.tsv"))
write_tsv(score_correlations, file.path(table_dir, "score_correlations.tsv"))
write_tsv(diet_collinearity %>% select(system, score, label, r2_diet_group, vif, vegans_at_zero),
          file.path(table_dir, "score_diet_group_collinearity.tsv"))

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Score_associations.png"), plot_associations, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```
